key_findings.detail:
Na⁺ drift in SiNx follows an Arrhenius relationship. Key activation energies measured:

- **Activation energy for Na⁺ drift through PECVD SiNx:** $E_a = 0.51$ eV (from corona bias-temperature stress experiments)
- [[papers/Elsevier-564-3774-2-s2.0-84940452054-2015-J-Drift characteristics of mobile ions in SiNx films and solar cells.pdf#page=2|Wilson et al. (2015), p.2]]

- **Activation energy for Na⁺ diffusion in SiN (leakage current):** $E_a = 0.93$ eV
- **Activation energy for Na atom out-diffusion (recovery):** $E_a = 0.96$ eV
- [[papers/IEEE-164-2299-2-s2.0-85087499813-2020-J-A Drift and Diffusion Model for PID-s in Solar Modules.pdf#page=2|Schulze et al. (2020), p.2]]

- **Activation energy for module-level leakage current (dry conditions):** $E_a = 0.809$ eV (glass: 0.814 eV, EVA: 0.782 eV)
- [[papers/IEEE-171-2371-2-s2.0-85099585463-2020-C-Modeling of Leakage Currents in c-Si PV Modules and Investigation of their Arrhenius Behavior.pdf#page=2|Spataru et al. (2020), p.2]]

Na⁺ drift in SiNx begins at approximately **50°C**, which overlaps with normal solar cell operating temperatures. This makes field-deployed modules continuously susceptible under normal operating conditions:
- [[papers/Elsevier-564-3774-2-s2.0-84940452054-2015-J-Drift characteristics of mobile ions in SiNx films and solar cells.pdf#page=1|Wilson et al. (2015), p.1]]

Degradation at 90°C is dramatically faster than at 49°C for the same applied voltage:

- Parameter controlling initial leakage current (c) increases **45-fold** from 49°C to 90°C
- Degradation arrival time (t₀) decreases **12-fold**
- Degradation completes in **1.73 hours at 90°C** vs. **40.2 hours at 49°C** (23× faster)
- [[papers/IEEE-164-2299-2-s2.0-85087499813-2020-J-A Drift and Diffusion Model for PID-s in Solar Modules.pdf#page=4|Schulze et al. (2020), p.4]]

The Al plate method (direct contact, low humidity) at 60°C produces PID **110 times faster** than conventional climate chamber testing at 60°C, 85% RH:
- [[papers/IOP-53-3675-2-s2.0-84956692262-2016-J-Consideration on Na diffusion and recovery phenomena in potential-induced degradation for crystallin.pdf#page=2|Masuda et al. (2016), p.2]]

Temperature dependence is strongly non-linear:
- Negligible PID degradation below **45°C**
- Severe degradation at **65°C and above** (for the same applied voltage)
- [[papers/Elsevier-541-3483-2-s2.0-84991699729-2016-J-Microscopic aspects of potential induced degradation phenomena and their recovery processes for p ty.pdf#page=2|Luo et al. (2016), p.2]]

At 85°C without any applied voltage bias, thermal diffusion alone causes a **2–3× reduction in carrier concentration** in CIGS cells. This is a reversible process (recovers on cooling), distinct from true electric-field-driven PID:
- [[papers/IEEE-267-2998-2-s2.0-85051002389-2018-J-Potential-Induced Degradation of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells: Alkali Metal Drift and Diffusion Effects.pdf#page=2|Theelen et al. (2018), p.2]]

For TOPCon PID-polarization, the thermal activation energy for degradation is $E_a = 0.71$ eV and for dark recovery is $E_a = 0.58$ eV:
- [[papers/Wiley-105-888-2-s2.0-85183130481-2024-J-Field-representative evaluation of PID-polarization in TOPCon PV modules by accelerated stress testi.pdf#page=2|Luo et al. (2024), p.2]]

Elevated stress conditions (60°C, 60% RH) cause **>90% efficiency loss** in perovskite cells, compared to **59% loss** at room conditions (25°C, 20% RH) under the same −1000 V stress:
- [[papers/Wiley-141-1314-2-s2.0-85153703868-2023-J-Study of Potential-Induced Degradation in Glass-Encapsulated Perovskite Solar Cells under Different .pdf#page=2|Nakka et al. (2023), p.2]]
